extracted.intended_audience: Nieman Foundation staff members, contractors, and freelance contributors to Nieman Journalism Lab, Nieman Reports, and Nieman Storyboard
extracted.subtask_description: Institutional policy governing when and how generative AI tools may be used in journalistic and editorial workflows for Nieman Foundation publications. Covers vetting, labeling, image usage, ethical concerns, and adherence to Harvard guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on publishing stories drafted or edited by generative AI
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not publish stories drafted or edited using generative AI tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that have been drafted or edited by generative AI must not be published. This is an absolute restriction meant to preserve editorial control and journalistic integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human vetting required for AI-derived materials
rubrics_metrics.description: A staff member or designated person will always vet the following material before it is published or incorporated into a story: information gathered through AI research tools; AI-generated transcriptions and translations; AI-generated text for social media posts or headlines; copyedits suggested by generative AI tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate a knowledgeable staff member to review and validate facts, translations, transcriptions, headlines, and suggested copyedits produced or informed by AI before use. Vetting must occur prior to publication or incorporation into editorial content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ban on AI-generated photorealistic depictions or alterations of real people/places
rubrics_metrics.description: We will not use AI image generators to create photorealistic depictions of real people or places, or to alter images of real people or places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not employ image-generation tools to fabricate or materially alter realistic photos of identifiable people or real locations. This prevents misleading readers and protects subjects from misrepresentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label and disclose AI-generated illustrations or composites
rubrics_metrics.description: Any AI-generated illustrations or composites we publish will be clearly labeled, and the image caption will disclose the method of generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When publishing non-photorealistic AI-generated visuals (illustrations, composites), include an explicit label and an image caption that explains how the image was generated. Ensure every visual serves a clear editorial purpose and does not mislead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear identification of all AI-generated material for readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Any AI-generated material in our publications or on our websites (images, translations, etc.) will be clearly identified for readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency: prominently disclose to audiences when content (images, translations, other assets) was created or substantially produced with AI tools. This is a cross-cutting requirement covering all published AI-derived content.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI must augment, not replace, human creativity and decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: AI should augment human creativity and decision-making, not replace it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AI as an assistive tool under human oversight. Maintain editorial judgment and final decision-making authority with human staff rather than delegating substantive editorial tasks to AI systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about AI use, especially for automated content
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency in how AI is used for content creation and decision-making is critical, especially when it comes to automated content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate clearly both internally and to audiences about the role and extent of AI in content processes. Extra care is required for fully or partially automated content-generation processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address ethical concerns (bias, IP, AI's role) up front
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical concerns such as bias, intellectual property, and AI’s role in content should be addressed upfront.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate and mitigate potential biases in AI outputs, ensure respect for copyright and IP when using AI-generated or AI-suggested material, and clarify the role AI played in producing content before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain quality and relevance despite AI-driven scale
rubrics_metrics.description: AI can help scale content creation, but quality and relevance must remain a top priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not sacrifice editorial quality, accuracy, or relevance for the sake of scaling production with AI. Use quality controls and human review to ensure standards are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use by digital content strategists for optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital content strategists may use AI to assess what content performs best and optimize content for targeted audiences as well as search engines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow data-driven AI tools in strategy and distribution roles (audience optimization, SEO) while ensuring any resulting content changes adhere to editorial and transparency rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freelance contributors must follow the policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All freelance contributors should familiarize themselves with these policies and follow them in their work for the Nieman Foundation and its publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freelancers are responsible for complying with the same vetting, labeling, and ethical standards as staff and contractors when producing content for Nieman.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human oversight as central principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Generative AI tools, overseen carefully by humans, can be useful and beneficial in parts of our workflow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt human oversight as a default for AI usage across workflows; treat AI outputs as provisional and subject to human validation aligned with journalistic principles of truth, accuracy, and transparency.
